title: Bain’s Bridge Data Centres Seeks to Upsize Loan to $6.6 Billion
source_used: Bloomberg text as carried by The Business Times (Singapore); Bloomberg page returns HTTP 403
key_facts: Bain Capital-owned Bridge Data Centres is in talks with banks to more than double an existing loan to about US$6.6 billion, people familiar said.

It would be one of the largest deals for the sector in Asia and extends an earlier effort to raise the loan to at least US$5 billion from the original US$2.8 billion obtained last year for its Malaysian operations.
The expanded deal could be launched into the market as early as November.
A loan of up to US$6 billion for a Thailand-based data centre has stalled, the people said, around the time Thailand decided last month to suspend construction of 49 data centres over energy use.
A Bridge spokesperson said it does not comment on unverified information or market speculation.

Moody's expects at least US$3 trillion to flow into data-centre-related investments over the next five years, mostly financed by debt; banks are increasingly mindful of exposure as they near lending limits.
Last week Firmus Grid pulled one of Australia's biggest-ever IPOs after difficulty convincing investors of its valuation.
quote_evidence: Bain Capital-owned Bridge Data Centres is in talks with banks to more than double the size of an existing loan to about US$6.6 billion, people familiar with the matter said, in what would be one of the largest deals for the sector in Asia.
The expanded deal could be launched into the market as early as November, according to the people, who asked not to be identified discussion private matters.
A spokesperson for Bridge said “as a matter of policy, we do not comment on unverified information or market speculation”.
why_it_matters_hint: Data-centre builders keep seeking much larger loans while banks near their limits and one Thai project stalls.
notes: Bloomberg original read through The Business Times, which carries Bloomberg's text (credited BLOOMBERG at the end). Unnamed sources; talks may change.
